summary: Set 114 S3 (terminal) put the step checklist in the surface the operator already has open. The Work Explorer's tree gained a FIFTH level: an in-flight session row expands to its steps -- the plan start_session seeded from spec.md, reconciled against what the orchestrator actually logged, with the same authored lifecycle glyphs the other rows use and '<- here' on the current step. It is the same list `python -m ai_router.session_checklist` prints, in the panel that is already open. This is the half Set 111 S4 recorded and deliberately did not build, on the grounds that it belonged to a session allowed to touch the rendering surface. Three limits are decisions rather than omissions, each journaled or tested: only the IN-FLIGHT session expands (every other session row stays a leaf -- the checklist answers 'where is this session', and it keeps the scan cost off the 45 sets that are not in progress); an absent, unreadable, wrong-session or empty ledger degrades to NO CHILDREN rather than a stale or invented list, and the row becomes a leaf rather than a twisty that opens onto nothing; and step rows carry no actions, with the menu-parity test asserting no `when` clause targets them so adding one later is a decision rather than a leak. THE ONE THING THIS SESSION DID THAT IT WAS WARNED ABOUT: the row-building rule now has two implementations, because the Explorer is TypeScript and the checklist is Python. Set 114 S2's own routed ai-assignment named that hazard for this session (L-069-1, the duplicate-parser defect this repo repeats most) and named the only acceptable mitigation -- 'port the rule with a shared fixture that proves the two agree row-for-row'. The alternative, spawning `python -m ai_router.session_checklist` on expand, was rejected on the record: it puts a process spawn on the expand path of a tree that refreshes on every watcher tick and a 30-second poll, and makes a DISPLAY feature fail whenever the interpreter or the package is unresolvable -- the exact coupling utils/migrateSessionState.ts was written to remove. So the mitigation shipped: ai_router/tests/fixtures/session-step-parity.json, twelve cases, asserted by test_step_row_parity.py against the real Python build_rows/read_spec_steps AND by sessionStepModel.test.ts against the TypeScript mirror. Change either implementation alone and a test fails; change the corpus alone and both fail. The corpus carries the cases that are easy to get wrong -- identity-before-ordinal claiming, a plan that moved under the session mid-flight (the L-112-1 planted defect: with ordinal matching left on, the last planned row silently vanishes), bookkeeping entries that must not claim a planned row, an append-only log that logged the same step twice, and a legacy set with no seeded plan at all. The scan-side lift is free by construction: readSessionSets already parses activity-log.json, so the only new I/O is one spec.md parse, on in-flight sets only, for the single question the renderer asks the spec (has the plan moved since registration?). Verification: round 1 discovery, both lenses (gpt-5.5, anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider), VERIFIED with zero findings. Suites after the last code change: pytest 3791 passed / 0 failed / 9 skipped (17m32s); Layer 3 Playwright 36 passed / 0 failed (9.8m), run because this session touches the Explorer rendering surface. One Layer 3 failure was found and fixed mid-session, and it was the test's fault rather than the product's: the e2e harness derives stepNumber as max+1, which lands PAST every seeded planned step and therefore always appends instead of claiming, so make-activity gained --step-number / --step-key / --status overrides with the defaults unchanged. Extension bumped 0.50.0 -> 0.51.0 (staged, publish operator-gated, superseding the never-published 0.50.0 and 0.49.0); ai_router stays 1.0.0 and was deliberately NOT bumped -- no router runtime code changed, and the only Python touched is test-support that pyproject excludes from the wheel.

uat.attestation: Operator, 2026-08-10: 'Right now, UAT is a broken, arduous process, which we shouldn't depend upon until Set 113 is finished. That said, I am going to authorize skipping UAT in this session. Please make a durable note of any features that you believe require UAT input. Later, I may create a remediation UAT set to address these things -- but only after set 113 is done. I am deferring because I think that set 113 will take some time to complete, and we need for this set, as well as set 115 to ship before 113.' The set declares requiresUAT: true and this session owed a guided-look walk; Set 113 (narrated video walkthroughs) has not landed, so the walk would have used the format the operator suspended once (Set 077) and waived once (Set 111 S4). Journaled as a verification REDUCTION under operator authority (decisions.jsonl, session 3) because it removes the operator-eyes layer this set's own spec armed. The waiver is not a write-off: the ten judgments that genuinely need eyes are itemized in docs/planning/uat-improvement-notes.md -> 'Deferred UAT -- owed judgments, by set', each naming what would decide it and the cheap remedy if the answer is no, so a remediation UAT set after Set 113 is authorable from that list alone. The two most likely to be wrong are flagged in the change log as well: the seeded step LABELS can read as ungrammatical fragments ('Work explorer expansion an in flight'), and blocked/failed steps borrow the cancelled glyph, which may read as 'this session was cancelled'.
